answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The vertex multiplier is published, charged in harbor, and trellis lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4337 identities would post 2120 proofs and burn roughly 24 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
